Indian Standard 

CODE OF PRACTICE FOR PACKAGING 
THERMAL INSULATION MATERIALS 

PART 1 SLABS, MATTRESSES AND PIPESECTIONS 
MADE OF FIBROUS MATERIALS 



UDC 62r798-2 : 662998 : 006-76 



© BIS 1991 

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 

March 1991 Price Group 1 



Packaging Codes Sectional Committee, LMD 26 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 8 May 1990, 
after the draft finalized by the Packaging Codes Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 

During transportation and handling, a bulky but light-weight product is liable to get damaged 
from excessive compressive loads. Some products, by their very nature, have limited resilience and 
can not recover their original form after being subjected to sustain crushing forces. It is, therefore, 
desired to design containers or cartons with the use of special materials and devices which will 
withstand whole or part of such compressive loads. 

The packaging materials and also the system as a whole must, therefore, be designed so as to 
provide structural rigidity at a low inherent weight. 



IS 13013 { Part 1 ) : 1990 



Indian Standard 



CODE OF PRACTICE FOR PACKAGING 
THERMAL INSULATION MATERIALS 

PARTI SLABS, MATTRESSES AND PIPESECTIOWS 
MADE OF FIBROUS MATERIALS 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part I ) covers the essential 
requirements for packaging of resin-bonded 
rockwool, slagwool and glasswool in form of 
slabs, mattresses or pipesections when trans- 
portation is carried out by rail or road. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standard is necessary 
adjunct to this standard; 

IS No, Title 

10556 : 1983 Code of practice for storage 
and handling of thermal insula- 
tion materials 

3 MATERIALS AND CONSTRUCTION 

3.1 The pack shall be a corrugated fibre board. 
The essential requirements for the different 
range of masses are given in Table 1. 

3.2 The manufacturer's joints shall be sealed 
with 50 mm sealing tape. Similar sealing shall 
be done on the top and bottom flaps. 

3.3 The package shall be reinforced with two 
non-metallic straps of 12 mm width along the 



girth direction of the box. The straps shall be 
clipped or heat sealed under tension. 

4 PACKAGING SEQUENCE 

4.1 The sequence of operations while packing 
the resin-bonded mineral wool, glasswool slabs 
or mattresses and pipe sections shall be as given 
below: 

a) The slabs or mattresses ( folded, if neces- 
sary ) shall be compressed by a mechanical 
device and compressed stack shall be slid 
into CFB box. 

b) Each pipesection, whether a half or a 
smaller section, shall be wrapped indivi- 
dually in a polyethylene film of suitable 
gauge and slid into CFB box. 

c) Top and bottom flaps shall be folded and 
sealed with sealing tapes. Stapled seams 
shall also be sealed with sealing tapes. 

d) Package shall be reinforced with two non- 
metallic straps along the girth. 

e) Package shall be legibly marked. 

5 STORAGE AND HANDLING 

5.1 The relevant requirements covered in IS 
10556 : 1983 shall be complied with.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the prowisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bnrean of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards AcU 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 

goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
